Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants should note that the Q&A session will be conducted via the telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables' results for the second quarter. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Lee, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Development Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Technology Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

First, on our development pipeline additions and project milestones, which highlight the robust momentum in our late-stage funnel and set us up for multi-year growth. Our pipeline serves as a key leading indicator for construction backlog and long-term contracted revenues, bolstered by tailwinds such as IRA tax credits, declining hardware costs, and rising corporate PPA demand. In Q2, we added a record 12.6 GW to our global development pipeline, reflecting a 45% increase quarter-over-quarter and 120% year-over-year growth, lifting our total gross pipeline to 58.2 GW spanning solar PV, wind, storage, and emerging areas like green hydrogen and long-duration energy storage. After decommissions of 1.8 GW—mostly early-stage projects falling short of our 12%+ unlevered IRR thresholds—our net pipeline reached 56.4 GW, with 72% in late-stage development ready for permitting or NTP, and 28% in early-stage greenfield efforts.

By technology, solar led with 7.2 GW of additions, or 57% of the total, featuring utility-scale bifacial PV using N-type TOPCon modules exceeding 23% efficiencies, akin to deployments by NextEra and First Solar. Wind contributed 3.1 GW, balanced between onshore in the US Midwest and offshore in the North Sea via Vestas partnerships for 15 MW+ platforms targeting capacity factors over 55%. Storage shone with 1.7 GW and 4.2 GWh, emphasizing standalone BESS and hybrid solar-plus-storage using four-hour LFP systems aiming for LCOS below $100/MWh. We also entered green hydrogen with 0.6 GW equivalent in electrolyzer capacity, anchored by our first 100 MW PEM project in Texas under the DOE's H2Hubs.

Regionally, the US accounted for 65% of adds at 8.2 GW, powered by IRA Section 45X credits and faster queues in PJM and ERCOT, cutting interconnection times by 18 months. The Southwest added 2.5 GW in Arizona and New Mexico, enhanced by dust mitigation and trackers for PRs above 28%. Europe saw 2.8 GW, targeting Germany's EEG auctions and UK's CfD Round 5, with our 500 MW Moray Firth offshore extension completing seabed surveys. APAC added 1.6 GW, driven by India's SECI tenders for 1 GW fixed-tilt solar in Rajasthan, aided by PLI incentives dropping module costs 15% YoY to under $0.22/W.

Key milestones included five PPAs totaling 2.1 GW, highlighted by an 850 MW solar-plus-storage agreement with Google for 24/7 carbon-free power at $32/MWh, aligning with EIA LCOE benchmarks. We secured permitting for 1.4 GW across three US projects, including full CPUC approval for the 600 MW Desert Bloom solar farm in California, enabling $150 million in PTC-eligible ITC adders for storage. Construction advanced with NTP on 900 MW, such as the 400 MW WindRiver onshore in Texas at 15% EPC completion with GE Vernova turbines for Q4 2025 COD at 14.5% IRR. Our 300 MW/1.2 GWh PJM battery hit mechanical completion early due to IRA-qualified LG Energy content. In clean tech, we reached FID on a 50 MW green hydrogen plant in Rotterdam with Air Products offtake, $120 million capex at 16% IRR post-EUH2 support.

These moves emphasize hybrids now at 40% of late-stage pipeline for grid stability and 20-30% PPA uplifts from frequency services, plus AI yield optimization via Enverus partnerships boosting P50 energies 5%. US manufacturing in Ohio (5 GW/year modules) and Corpus Christi turbine yards stabilize costs at $0.28/Wdc. We anticipate 10-15 GW adds in H2, 25% annual pipeline-to-backlog conversion, leveraging $20 billion liquidity and $5 billion green bond revolver for 15-20% FCF CAGR through 2028, ahead of peers like Ørsted and Brookfield.

Second, the substantial impact of government incentives and subsidies, which fueled about 28% of our Q2 revenue, up from 22% last year, adding roughly 450 basis points to adjusted EBITDA margins. Globally, post-COP28 commitments exceed $1.7 trillion through 2030 per BloombergNEF. The US IRA drives $370 billion in investments; our solar and storage qualified for full 30% ITC plus 10% domestic content, reaching 40% effective on $2.1 billion deployed, like the 500 MW SunForge in Texas gaining a 10% Energy Community bonus for $210 million tax equity via BlackRock JVs.

PTCs benefited our 1.2 GW Midwest onshore wind at $25/MWh indexed to 2.8% inflation, yielding $185 million cash in Q2 and 15% FCF growth; paired with TerraStore BESS, we tap 50% ITC for six-hour storage. In Europe, our 800 MW German/Spanish portfolio captured €450 million merit-order premiums under REPowerEU, with CBAM adding €85/ton CO2 edge for our TOPCon modules over Longi/JinkoSolar, growing EU backlog 35% YoY to €3.2 billion at 28% margins. APAC saw A$150 million from Australia's LRET and Japan's fund for 300 MW floating solar, plus India's PLI covering 50% of 2 GW Gujarat gigafactory capex for $22/MWh LCOE.

Incentives are declining from 40% of capex in 2020 to 25% by 2027 per IRENA as PPAs fall to $20/MWh in ERCOT; ours dropped from 65% to 45% via corporate PPAs with Google/Microsoft for RE100. We counter subsidy risks with $1.2 billion ITC/PTC transfers at 95 cents/dollar to JPMorgan, $5.2 billion 2025 capture pre-PTC phase-out, perovskite tandems at 32.5% efficiency, and SEIA/GWEC lobbying. These added $620 million to Q2 revenue, 12% EPS boost, securing $15.4 billion backlog at 92% visibility for durable 15% IRRs by 2027.

Third, advancements in tax equity financing and project-level financing, vital for scaling our 5.2 GW operating assets and 12 GW pipeline in the post-IRA era with storage and bifacial PV. Tax equity from banks like JPMorgan, Goldman, US Bancorp monetizes ITC/PTC/48E credits at 30-70% effective via flip structures yielding investors 6-8% IRR before residual flip. Q2 closed $1.2 billion, including $750 million with Bank of America for 450 MW Desert Sun hybrid in Imperial Valley at 70% ITC stack (10% domestic First Solar Series 7, 20% Tesla Megapack), 7.2% investor yield amid $25 billion market liquidity. YTD $3.8 billion across 2.1 GW cut all-in capital costs to 4.1%, US-focused but shifting to green bonds/PABs in Europe for 1.2 GW Polish offshore JV with Ørsted.

Diversifying with MetLife, Hannon Armstrong, and $400 million IRA 6418 transfers to Google speeds timelines 6-9 months for 800 MW ERCOT batteries Q1 2025 FID. Project-level non-recourse debt/back-leverage keeps corporate leverage at 2.1x; Q2 $900 million from MUFG/SocGen for 300 MW Illinois wind at SOFR+145bps (5.8% all-in), 65% advance, post-COD LMIR+110bps, plus $250 million Apollo back-leverage recycling $180 million for M&A like SunPower tuck-in. Debt is 40% of stack at 5.2% average, 18-year tenors; APAC uses Mizuho JPY green loans for Singapore floating solar.

Hybrid funding (40-50% tax equity, 40% debt, sponsor rest) yields 4.8% WACC, >12% ROIC. Mitigating TOPCon shortages via DOE Nevada gigafactory offtake; $5.5 billion 2025 pipeline ($2.2B tax equity, $3.3B debt) for 20% growth with IRA extensions.

Fourth, exceptional capacity factor performance across solar, wind, and storage, with fleet-wide blended CF at 32.4%, up 8% YoY from 30.0% and beating 31.5% guidance, adding $45 million to EBITDA or 2.5 margin points. Solar (42% portfolio, 12.3 GWac) hit 26.8%, +6.7% YoY; newer trackers (Array DuraTrack HZ v3 on 40%) >29% vs. 22% fixed-tilt, bifacial Jinko Tiger Pro +1.5-2pp, AI soiling reduction 15%. US Southwest 28.5% (7.2 kWh/m² GHI), ERCOT 27.1% with BESS, Australia 24.2%, Europe 22.1% but +10% perovskites. 7.8% above NREL 24.9%; $250M repower 1.5 GW HJT for 28-30% by 2026.

Wind (38%, 14.8 GW): onshore 37.2% (+5.2% YoY), offshore 49.1% (+7.8%), beating IRENA. Vestas V136 repowers +12%, Siemens Gamesa offshore 11.2 m/s, wake steering -3-5% losses. US Midwest 38.9%, Europe offshore 50.2%; $400M repowers including GE Vernova.

Storage (20%, 4.2 GWh/1.8 GW): 68.4% utilization (+11% YoY), 92.7% RTE; Tesla Megapack VPP 1.2 cycles/day, LFP 1.2% degradation. ERCOT 75.2%, CAISO 62.1%, UK 72%; 15% above EIA via hybrids. $600M iron-air for 80%+ utilization, <$80/MWh LCOS.

O&M downtime <1.5%, $1.3B tech spend; FY24 CF 33.5-34.5% for 15-18% EBITDA growth, > peers.

Fifth, gross margin and operating margin trends showing resilience. Gross margin reached 28.5%, +320bps YoY from 25.2%, +150bps QoQ from 27.0%, TTM 27.8% beating 26.5% consensus. Vertical integration: Arizona perovskite-TOPCon fab cuts CTM to 1.2%, +25W/panel; poly-Si $8-10/kg via Tongwei/GCL. ESS mix 35% revenue (>35% margins vs. 24% PERC), Arizona 5 GWh 95% utilization $112/kWh (-18% YoY). US 31.2% (IRA adders), Europe 26.8% (CBAM), APAC 25.4%.

Op margin 12.3% (+250bps YoY), TTM 11.9%; OpEx +8% YoY to $145M (14.2% revenue), R&D 4.1% on sodium-ion/H2. Forex $12M, IRA $18M, AI procurement -25% cycles, Boulder IP $25M. 'Resilient Renewables': 60% US/EU fabs, ESS/hybrids; FY25 gross 29-30%, op 13-15%.

Sixth, our strategic priorities and outlook. Q2 revenue $1.35B +28% YoY, FY $5.2B +35%, EBITDA margins 32%. Pillars: solar+storage (75% $18.5B backlog, 12 GWdc PPAs like 1.2 GW Texas IRR 12.5%, $0.22/W First Solar); Q1 2025 1.5 GWdc, FY 6 GWdc/3 GWh $4.8B +40%, 30-33% margins Aurora optimizer.

Next-gen: 20% $2.1B capex on iron-air (500 MWh PPA <$50/MWh), H2 50 MW LA $2.50/kg Air Products, Bloom SOEC. Regions: NA 80% (Ohio 5 GW fab), Europe 2 GW Irish wind €55/MWh Ørsted, Australia 400 MW BESS 15% IRR, India 300 MW Adani. Q1 guide $1.5-1.6B rev, $450-480M EBITDA, FY $7.0-7.3B +35-40%, 33-35% margins, $2.1B capex, <2.5x leverage; 10 GW/year by 2028 $12B rev 35% margins >20% ROE.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q2. Revenue was $1.35 billion, a 28% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 28.5%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $145 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $180 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel for an update on our project pipeline.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 56.4 GW of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Lisa Wong will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite-silicon tandems at 32.5% efficiency, energy storage solutions such as iron-air flow batteries for 100-hour dispatch, and smart grid technologies with AI-driven forecasting and virtual power plants. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of our next-generation perovskite-enhanced TOPCon modules is expected to boost energy yields by up to 10% and reduce LCOE across future projects.

And now, Elena Vasquez will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management—such as targeting net-zero operations by 2030 and achieving 100% renewable sourcing for our facilities. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability, including job creation in energy communities and biodiversity programs around project sites. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense, enhancing stakeholder value and regulatory goodwill.

I'll now turn the call back to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. In closing, we are confident that Solara Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, John. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall, particularly in the US where IRA implementation has streamlined queues in PJM and ERCOT, reducing timelines by up to 18 months, and CPUC approvals like Desert Bloom show permitting momentum. In Europe, REPowerEU and CfD auctions in the UK/Germany are accelerating offshore and solar, though CBAM adds trade edges. APAC varies—India's PLI and SECI are strong, Australia's LRET reliable—but we navigate local content rules via partnerships. We're proactively engaging via SEIA and GWEC to extend PTC/ITC amid policy risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Lisa Wong:
Great question, Maria. Integration challenges like grid curtailment and duration are core to our hybrid focus—40% of late-stage pipeline now. We're deploying LFP Megapack-like systems with VPP software for 1.2 cycles/day and 92.7% RTE, co-locating 70% with solar/wind for arbitrage and RA compliance. Next-gen iron-air from Form Energy hits 100 hours for <$80/MWh LCOS, and sodium-ion pilots cut costs 15%. AI optimizes dispatch, as in ERCOT scarcity at $250/MWh, positioning us for 80%+ utilization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Jordan Lee:
David, we're bullish—the global market should see 15-20% CAGR through 2030 per BloombergNEF's $1.7T spend, driven by decarbonization, RE100 corporates, and falling LCOE to $20-25/MWh unsubsidized. Solara targets 20% capacity growth via 56 GW pipeline, 10 GW/year deployments by 2028, $12B revenue at 35% margins. Hybrids, H2, and regional diversification de-risk us beyond subsidies.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for any closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Solara Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
